plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: A bushy perennial cultivated for thousands of years, producing dense, layered flower heads in a wide range of forms from pompons to spiders. It is a mainstay of autumn gardens across the Northern Hemisphere and thrives in the cool temperatures of late October.
plants.location: East Asia origin; widely cultivated in temperate gardens in North America, Europe, Japan, and China
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums are the official flower of November birthdays and are the emblem of the Japanese Imperial family, whose throne is called the Chrysanthemum Throne.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tall, semi-deciduous tree with fern-like leaves that erupts in masses of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. Spring in the Southern Hemisphere brings its peak bloom, carpeting streets and parks with fallen blossoms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring (October to November in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to South America; planted in Australia, South Africa (Pretoria), Argentina, and New Zealand's northern regions
plants.funFact: Pretoria in South Africa is nicknamed the Jacaranda City because of its roughly 70,000 jacaranda trees, which turn the city purple every October.

plants.name: Callicarpa americana
plants.description: A deciduous shrub of the southeastern United States whose small pinkish flowers appear in summer, but in late October it is most noted for its clusters of vivid purple berries. Some related species and late-flowering garden plants share autumn interest with it, making it a fixture in fall landscapes.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer flowers, with fruit display peaking in autumn
plants.location: Southeastern United States, Mexico, and the Caribbean
plants.funFact: Crushed beautyberry leaves have traditionally been rubbed on skin as a mosquito repellent, and research has found compounds in them that repel insects.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub that opens fragrant, delicate flowers in autumn, earlier than the more familiar Camellia japonica. Its blooms attract late-season pollinators and brighten gardens when most other plants are fading.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to early winter (October to December)
plants.location: Native to Japan; grown in the southeastern United States, Japan, the Mediterranean, and Australia
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is a close relative of the tea plant, and its seeds are pressed to produce camellia oil used in cooking and cosmetics.
